old: \citet{FKS26} ask: ``We ask whether distribution-independent SQ learning implies low dimension complexity''. The answer is negative. reason: A1: exact SGD update, index endpoints, expectation and architecture quantifiers.
old: Each layer-$i$ weight is initialized independently with law $N(0,1/n_{i-1})$. One fixed step size is used for $T$ online updates on fresh examples with logistic loss $\log(1+e^{-yf_\theta(x)})$. The output is the sign of the sum of the final half of the iterates. The architecture, step size and horizon are fixed for the class before the marginal and target. Open Question 1 asks whether a common expected-error guarantee at $\epsilon<1/4$ forces $\dc(H)\le CTS$, or a polynomial bound in $(T,S)$. This question remains open here.
new:
Here $n_0=n$ and $n_L=1$. Each layer-$i$ weight is initialized independently with law $N(0,1/n_{i-1})$. With one fixed step size $\eta$, for $t=0,\ldots,T-1$ draw $x^{(t)}\sim D$ independently and set
\[
 \theta^{(t+1)}=\theta^{(t)}-\eta\nabla_\theta
 \ell\!\left(h^*(x^{(t)})f_{\theta^{(t)}}(x^{(t)})\right),
 \qquad \ell(z)=\log(1+e^{-z}).
\]
The returned predictor is
\[
 \widehat h(x)=\sign\!\left(\sum_{t=\lceil T/2\rceil}^{T}f_{\theta^{(t)}}(x)\right).
\]
The architecture, step size and horizon are fixed for the class before $D$ and $h^*$. Open Question 1 of \citet[Section~2]{FKS26} asks whether a guarantee $\E L_{D,h^*}(\widehat h)\le\epsilon<1/4$ for every $D,h^*$, with expectation over both initialization and online sampling, forces $\dc(H)\le CTS$. Their Section~4 also asks for a polynomial bound in $(T,S)$. This question remains open here.
